metadata.source: Pdt. Durgaprasad and Kasinath Pandurang Parab, Kavyamala [old, cumulative series], vol. 1, 1886 (3rd ed., 1929), pp. 79-90.

body.translated_text: The <s>Prāṇābharaṇa</s> (Ornament of Life) composed by the king of scholars, the illustrious <s>Jagannātha</s>, together with his own commentary.

children.text: vidvāṃso vasudhātale paravacaḥślāghāsu vācaṃyamā bhūpālāḥ kamalāvilāsamadironmīlanmadāghūrṇitāḥ /
children.translated_text: The learned ones on the surface of the earth are restrained in speech regarding praise of another's words; kings are reeling with intoxication from the sportive play of <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>);

children.text: āsye ghāsyati kasya lāsyamadhunā dhanyasya kāmālasasvarvāmādharamādhurīmadharayanvācāṃ vilāso mama || 1 ||
children.translated_text: in whose mouth is the dance [of my words] now fortunate? The playfulness of my words, yielding the sweetness of the lower lip of the heavenly beauty, languid with desire! [JPran_1]

body.text:
vidvāṃsa ityādi prāyadarśanābhiprāyametat /
tena sahṛdayairna manāgapi vimanāyitavyam /

children.translated_text: And this is <s>bhāvadhvani</s> (suggestion of a transitory emotion),

because of the predominant expression of the poet's anxiety, whose foundation (<s>ālambana</s>) is the meaning conveyed in the latter half [of the verse], and whose <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent) is the composition of this verse.
The figure of <s>vyatireka</s> (distinction), in which neither term of comparison is taken up [explicitly], is the evident ornament.
The languor of desire intensifies the sweetness of the lower lip of the <s>vāmā</s> (beautiful woman).

body.translated_text: The words 'vidvāṃsaḥ' (the learned) and so forth express what is generally observed. Therefore connoisseurs (<s>sahṛdaya</s>) should not be disheartened in the slightest.

children.text: vidrāṇaiva guṇajñatā samudito bhūyānasūyābharaḥ kālo 'yaṃ kalirājagāma jagatīlāvaṇyakukṣiṃbhariḥ /
children.translated_text: Appreciation of merit has indeed fled; an excessive burden of envy has arisen; this is the age of <s>Kali</s> that has come — a glutton consuming the beauty of the world.

children.text: evaṃ bhāvanayā madīyakavite maunaṃ kimālambase jāgartu kṣitimaṇḍale ciramiha śrīkāmarūpeśvaraḥ || 2 ||
children.translated_text: Thus reflecting, O my poem, why do you resort to silence? May the lord of illustrious <s>Kāmarūpa</s> remain wakeful in the circle of the earth for long! [JPran_2]
From here onward, this same [bhāvadhvani] will continue up to the final verse.

children.text: asya cātra maunānubhāvito varṇanīyālambano nirvedo guṇa iti preyolaṃkārāspadam /
children.translated_text: And here, <s>nirveda</s> (world-weariness) whose foundation is the subject to be described [i.e., the king], manifested through the <s>anubhāva</s> of silence — being a subordinate quality (<s>guṇa</s>) — is the locus of the figure <s>preyas</s> (the predominance of a bhāva).

And here, since the poem (<s>kavitā</s>), being inanimate, [is addressed as if animate,] the superimposition of consciousness upon the non-conscious is intended — this is <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) in the form of an [impossible] relation.
Therefore, there is no impropriety in [attributing] reflection, silence, <s>nirveda</s>, and the act of direct address [to the poem].

body.translated_text: This is <s>bhāvadhvani</s> (suggestion of an emotion) of the <s>rati</s> (love) of the poet directed toward the king.

children.translated_text: By the lions, swooping forth from within the mountain-cave depths of the earth, having their eye-corners startled and trembling from the offense of the disturbance of their sleep,

bold in its contempt of the sound of the storm clouds rising at the time of your departure — the sound of the pair of battle drums, rubbing against the shore of the ocean of milk, is victorious in the world! [JPran_3]

body.text: atra rājālambanasya tādṛśanādaśravaṇoddīpitasya nayanapracalanānubhāvitasya giriguhāgarbhotpatanābhivyaktenāmarṣeṇa saṃcāriṇā paripoṣitasya pārīndragatotsāhasya sthāyino rājaviṣayakaratibhāvāṅgatvādrasālaṃkāratvam /

children.translated_text: As they have said —
'Where <s>rasa</s> and the like are subordinate elements',
whether the primary sentence-meaning is something else [or not] — in such poetry, <s>rasa</s> and the like are ornaments (<s>alaṃkāra</s>) — this is my view.'

body.translated_text: Here, the permanent emotion (<s>sthāyī</s>) of <s>utsāha</s> (enthusiasm) belonging to the lions — whose <s>ālambana</s> (foundation) is the king, whose <s>uddīpana</s> (excitant) is the hearing of such a sound, whose <s>anubhāva</s> is the trembling of the eyes, and which is nourished by the <s>saṃcārī</s> (transitory emotion) of <s>amarṣa</s> (indignation) manifested through leaping from the depths of mountain caves — being subordinate to the <s>rati</s> directed toward the king, this is <s>rasālaṃkāra</s> (an ornament of rasa).

children.translated_text: By the word 'ghṛṣṭā' (rubbing against), it is conveyed that such a sound, being obstructed by the coastal mountains, did not go further;
otherwise, it is implied that it would have reached even the <s>Lokāloka</s> mountain.
It is not said 'mṛṣṭa' (polished/touched),
because in that case there would follow the implication of slackness.

body.translated_text: In the third and fourth quarters, the figures of <s>vyatireka</s> (distinction) and <s>atiśaya</s> (hyperbole) are clearly evident.

children.text: kiṃ brūmastava vīratāṃ vayamamī yasmindharākhaṇḍala krīḍākuṇḍalitabhru śoṇanayanaṃ dormaṇḍalaṃ paśyati /
children.translated_text: What shall we say of your heroism, O lord of the earth, when these [warriors] behold your arm-circle, with playfully arched brow, with reddened eyes,
at that very moment the trees growing in the cave-dwellings of the <s>Vindhya</s> forests are illuminated by thousands of ornaments, denser [in brilliance] than rows of ruby necklaces! [JPran_4]

children.text: atra vindhyāraṇyagatānāṃ guhāgṛhāṇāmavaniruhāṃ ca vindhyagatānāṃ guhāgṛhāṇāmaraṇyagatānāmavaniruhāṇāṃ vā bhūṣaṇena kāryeṇāprastutena tvadarinārīṇāṃ svanagarāṇi parityajya niśi guhāgṛheṣu tarutaleṣu ca vinyasya sakalābharaṇāni kṛtaśayanānāṃ prātastvadāgamanasaṃbhrameṇa tatkarmakaṃ vismaraṇaṃ bhāravaśātparityāgo vā prastuto gamyata ityaprastutapraśaṃsā /
children.translated_text: Here, by the ornaments — an irrelevant effect — adorning the trees and cave-dwellings in the <s>Vindhya</s> forests (or the cave-dwellings of <s>Vindhya</s> and the trees of the forests), the relevant [meaning] is conveyed: that the wives of your enemy-kings, having abandoned their own cities at night and lying down in cave-dwellings and beneath trees with all their ornaments placed [around them], in the morning's haste upon your arrival, either forgot to perform that [collection of ornaments], or abandoned them due to their weight — thus this is <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant).
However, if the effect is somehow relevant, then the figure would be <s>paryāyokta</s> (indirect expression).

children.text: māhātmyasya paro 'vadhirnijagṛhaṃ gambhīratāyāḥ pitā ratnānāmahameka eva bhuvane ko vāparo mādṛśaḥ /
children.translated_text: The ultimate limit of greatness, the father of profundity, I alone on earth am [the repository] of gems — who else is like me?

children.text: ityevaṃ paricintya mā sma sahasā garvāndhakāraṃ gamo dugdhābdhe bhavatā samo vijayate śrīprāṇanārāyaṇaḥ || 5 ||
children.translated_text: Having thus reflected, O milk-ocean, do not rashly enter the darkness of pride — the illustrious <s>Prāṇanārāyaṇa</s> is victorious, being equal to you! [JPran_5]

Here, the type of the figure <s>pratīpa</s> (reversal) has as its basis the similarity characterized by the object of comparison [being told] to set aside the pride arising from its special quality, which would preclude a similarity [with the subject].
And some say this is a variety of <s>upamā</s> (simile).
Others [say it is] distinct, due to the distinctiveness of its aesthetic charm.

children.text: tattvo janma sitāṃśuśekharatanujyotsnānimagnātmano dugdhāmbhonidhimugdhavīcivalayaiḥ sākaṃ parikrīḍanam /
children.translated_text: The truth is: your birth is from [someone with] the crescent moon on his head; your play is with the waves of the ocean of milk, immersed in the moonlight of the daughter of the son of the white-rayed one [moon];

children.text: saṃvāsaḥ suralokasindhupuline vādaḥ sudhāṃśoḥ karaiḥ kasmānnojjvalimānamañcatutamāṃ deva tvadīyaṃ yaśaḥ || 6 ||
children.translated_text: your dwelling is on the shore of the celestial river; your discourse is with the rays of the nectar-rayed [moon] — then why does your fame not ascend to [even greater] brilliance, O lord? [JPran_6]

children.text: atra yaśasi dhavalatātiśayastaddharmisaṃbandhaprayuktatvena kathita iti samasya viṣayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the excess of whiteness in fame, being stated as caused by its connection with that property-bearer, is the domain of <s>samasya</s> (a type of poetic challenge).

children.text: aṃśukṛtaścandre tatkṛtaśca bhagavati bhagavatkṛtaśca rājanītyevamuttarottaramupacīyamāno rājagata utkarṣaḥ pratīyata iti sāraviṣayaḥ //
children.translated_text: The excellence pertaining to the king, being cumulatively increased — produced by the ray in the moon, by the moon in the Lord [Śiva], and by the Lord in the king — is perceived as suggestive; thus it is the domain of the essential (<s>sāra</s>).

children.text: ābadhnāsyalakānnirasyasitamāṃ colaṃ rasākāṅkṣayā laṅkāyāvaśatāṃ tanoṣi kuruṣe jaṅghālalāṭakṣatam /
children.translated_text: You untie the locks of hair, you loosen the sides of the garment, with desire for pleasure you bring <s>Laṅkā</s> to subjection, you inflict bruises on the shin and forehead,

children.text: pratyaṅgaṃ parimardanirdayamaho cetaḥ samālambase vāmānāṃ viṣaye nṛpendra bhavataḥ prāgalbhyamadbhutam || 7 ||
children.translated_text: you forcefully massage every limb — alas! The boldness you exhibit, O king of kings, in the domain of beautiful women, is astonishing! [JPran_7]

children.text: atra prakṛtidharmigatayoḥ prakṛtāprakṛtayoḥ prakṛtayoreva vā vṛttāntayoḥ śleṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here there is <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) between two narratives — either of the real subject and a different subject, or of the relevant and the irrelevant, or of two relevant [meanings].

children.text: sa ca ṣaṭsu sthaleṣu śabdanānātvanibandhano dvayoścārthanānātvanibandhanaḥ /
children.translated_text: And it is based on the difference of words in six places, and on the difference of meaning in two.
The ancients say both of these are verbal ornaments (<s>śabdālaṃkāra</s>).

The first is a verbal ornament because of verbal paronomasia, by the principle of lac and wood [inseparably joined]; the second is a meaning-ornament because of semantic paronomasia, by the principle of two fruits on a single stalk — thus the moderns.

children.text: deva tvāṃ paritaḥ stavantu kavayo lobhena kiṃ tāvatā stavyastvaṃ bhavitāsi yasya taruṇaścāpapratāpo 'niśam /
children.translated_text: O lord, let poets praise you all around out of greed — what of that? You shall remain praiseworthy, whose youthful valor's heat, unceasingly,

children.text: kroḍāntaḥ kurutetarāṃ vasumatīmāśāḥ samāliṅgati dyāṃ cumbatyamarāvatī ca sahasā gacchatyagamyāmapi || 8 ||
children.translated_text: takes the earth within its embrace, clasps the directions [in its arms], kisses the sky, and goes swiftly even to <s>Amarāvatī</s> (the city of the gods), though she is unapproachable! [JPran_8]

children.text: atra pratāpagataḥ pṛthivyādisaṃbandho liṅgaviśeṣāvacchinnatattatsādhāraṇaviśeṣaṇābhivyaktakāmukavṛttāntābhinnatayā sthita iti samāsoktiḥ kāryarūpadharmaprayuktaśuddhasādhāraṇyena viśeṣaṇasāmyamālambya pravṛttā /
children.translated_text: Here, the connection of valor with the earth and so forth stands as undifferentiated from the narrative of a lover, manifested through qualifications that are common [to both subjects] and delimited by specific grammatical genders — thus this is <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression), proceeding by relying on the equality of qualifications through pure commonality of effect-form properties.
And this, because of giving rise to censure-based elevation, is a quality (<s>guṇa</s>) within [the figure of] <s>avyājastuti</s> (unfeigned praise).

children.text: lokānāṃ vipadaṃ dhunoṣi kuruṣe saṃpattimatyutkaṭāmityalpetarajalpitairjaḍadhiyāṃ bhūpāla mā gā madam /
children.translated_text: You dispel the misfortunes of people, you bestow exceedingly abundant prosperity — O king, do not become proud from such trifling prattle of the dull-witted.

children.text: yatkīrtistava vallabhā laghutarabrahmāṇḍabhāṇḍodare piṇḍīkṛtya mahonnatāmapi tanuṃ kaṣṭena hā vartate || 9 ||
children.translated_text: For your fame, O beloved, in the small vessel of the egg of <s>Brahmā</s>, having compressed even her exceedingly lofty body, alas, remains with difficulty! [JPran_9]
Here too, as before [avyājastuti applies].

Furthermore, the figure <s>sādhika</s> (excess), through the construction of smallness of one [entity] resulting from the proof of the extensiveness of the other among container and contained, is also a quality (<s>guṇa</s>) within that [avyājastuti].

children.text: kṣoṇīṃ śāsati mayyupadravalavaḥ kasyāpi na syāditi prauḍhaṃ vyāharato vacastava kathaṃ deva pratīmo vayam /
children.translated_text: While I govern the earth, no one shall have the slightest power of oppression — how can we believe these bold words of yours, O lord?

children.text: pratyakṣaṃ bhavato vipakṣanivahairdyāmutpatadbhiḥ krudhā yadyuṣmatkulakoṭimūlapuruṣo nirbhidyate bhāskaraḥ || 10 ||
children.translated_text: For it is directly perceived that the sun, the primeval ancestor of the root of your dynasty's millions, is pierced by the hosts of your enemies flying up to the sky in rage! [JPran_10]

body.translated_text: Here, that [<s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise)] is not embraced by either <s>adhika</s> (excess) or <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression).

children.text: āsvādena raso rasena kavitā kāvyena vaṇī tayā lokāntaḥkaraṇānurāgarasikaḥ sabhyaḥ sabhā cāmunā /
children.translated_text: Through savoring, there is <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic flavor); through <s>rasa</s>, poetry; through poetry, eloquence; through it, the cultured audience becomes a connoisseur of the inner heart's affection; and through him, the assembly —

children.text: dāridryānaladahyamānajagatīpīyūṣadhārādhara kṣoṇīnātha tathā bhavāṃśca bhavatā bhūmaṇḍalaṃ bhāsate || 11 ||
children.translated_text: O lord of the earth, rain-cloud of nectar-streams [quenching] the world burning in the fire of poverty — thus both you and the circle of the earth shine through you! [JPran_11]
This is <s>mālādīpaka</s> (chain-illumination), say the ancients.

children.text: dīpakasya sādṛśyamūlakatāniyamānna mālādīpakamapi tvekāvalībheda iti tu vayam //
children.translated_text: Since <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination) is restricted to being rooted in similarity, it is not <s>mālādīpaka</s> either; rather, it is a variety of <s>ekāvalī</s> (single-strand) — this is our view.

children.text: amlāyanyadarātikairavakulānyamlāsiṣuḥ satvaraṃ dainyadhvāntakadambakāni parito neśustamāṃ tāmasāḥ /
children.translated_text: The clusters of night-lotuses of the enemies wilt; the masses of darkness of wretchedness quickly perish; all the <s>tāmasas</s> (darkness-beings/those of dull nature) have vanished;

children.text: sanmārgāḥ prasaranti sādhunalinānyullāsamātanvate tanmanye bhavataḥ pratāpatapano deva prabhātonmukhaḥ || 12 ||
children.translated_text: the right paths extend; the lotuses of the good bloom forth in delight — I think, O lord, that your valor-sun is approaching dawn! [JPran_12]

body.translated_text: Here, the inference whose mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is produced by <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), due to the absence of an [actual] cause, and due to the impossibility of <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), becomes a statement of inference (<s>anumiti</s>).

children.text: utkṣiptāḥ kabarībharaṃ vivalitāḥ pārśvadvayaṃ nyakkṛtāḥ pādāmbhojayugaṃ ruṣā parihṛtā dūreṇa celāñcalam /
children.translated_text: Tossed up is the mass of hair, turned aside are both sides [of the garment], pressed down are the pair of lotus-feet, cast far away in anger is the hem of the garment;

children.text: gṛhṇanti tvarayā bhavatpratibhaṭakṣmāpālavāmabhruvāṃ yāntīnāṃ gahaneṣu kaṇṭakacitāḥ ke ke na bhūmīrūhāḥ || 13 ||
children.translated_text: they seize [the fleeing women] with haste — is there any tree in the dense forests, bristling with thorns, that does not [seize] the wives of your rival kings, with their frowning brows, as they flee? [JPran_13]

body.text: atra kaṇṭakacitatvena kabarīgrahaṇādeḥ saṃkīrṇatvātkāryadharmāntarā saṃkīrṇaśuddhasādhāraṇyena viśeṣaṇasāmyamālambya pravṛttā samāsoktiḥ //
body.translated_text: Here, because the grasping of the braid (<s>kabarīgrahaṇa</s>) etc. is mixed with the [meaning of] being studded with thorns (<s>kaṇṭaka</s>), [the figure is] <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression), which has proceeded by taking recourse to the similarity of qualifiers (<s>viśeṣaṇasāmya</s>) through the commonality — whether mixed or pure — of properties belonging to different effects. //

children.text: dṛṣṭiḥ saṃbhṛtamaṅgalā budhamayī deva tvadīyā sabhā kāvyasyāśrayabhūtamāsyamaruṇādhāro 'dharaḥ sundaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Your gaze is full of auspiciousness, your court (<s>sabhā</s>) is constituted of <s>Budha</s> (Mercury / the wise), O Lord; the lip, which is the abode of poetry (<s>kāvya</s>), is beautiful, a support for the ruddy [glow] (<s>aruṇa</s>);

children.text: krodhaste 'śanimūrudāradhiṣaṇa svāntaṃ tu somāspadaṃ rājannūnamanūnavikrama bhavānsarvagrahālambanam || 14 ||
children.translated_text: Your anger is the thunderbolt (<s>aśani</s>), O one of mighty thighs and noble intellect; your heart is the abode of the moon (<s>Soma</s>). O King of unfailing valor, you are truly the support of all <s>grahas</s> (planets / sense-faculties)! // <s>JPran</s>_14 //

body.text: atrotprekṣyamānasarvagrahālambanatvasya samānādhikaraṇeṣu dharmeṣu tattadgrahāśritāṅgakatveṣu viśeṣaṇībhūtaistattadgrahaiḥ saha viṣayasya rājño kalyāṇāśrayatvādiṣu viśeṣaṇānāṃ kalyāṇādīnāṃ śleṣeṇābhedasaṃpādanadvārā tādṛśadharmasādhāraṇatāsaṃpattau tannimittakotprekṣāsiddhiḥ //
body.translated_text: Here, the property of being the support of all <s>grahas</s> (<s>sarvagrahālambanatva</s>) that is being fancifully imagined (<s>utprekṣā</s>) — since the co-referential properties [of the king] serve as the substrates of the respective <s>grahas</s> (planets), and the qualifiers [such as] auspiciousness etc. of the subject (the king) are identified through <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) with the respective <s>grahas</s> that serve as qualifiers — through this device of producing non-difference, the commonality of such properties is achieved, and thereby the <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) based on that is established. //

children.text: sṛṣṭiḥ sṛṣṭibhuvā purā kila paritrātuṃ jaganmaṇḍalaṃ tvaṃ caṇḍātapanirdayaṃ tapasi yajjvālājaṭālaiḥ karaiḥ /
children.translated_text: In ancient times, in order to protect the circle of the world, the creation was created by the Creator; you, merciless with fierce heat, in your <s>tapas</s> (penance/heat), with rays that are blazing matted locks —

children.text: saṃrambhāruṇalocano raṇabhuvi prasthātukāmo 'dhunā jānīmo bhavatā na hanta viditaḥ śrīkāmarūpeśvaraḥ || 15 ||
children.translated_text: With eyes reddened by fury, now desiring to set forth on the battlefield — we know, alas, the Lord of <s>Kāmarūpa</s> is not recognized by you! // <s>JPran</s>_15 //

body.text: atra rājavarṇanāṅgatvena raverbhayotpādane varṇyatvena prastute sākṣāttadananuguṇatvenāprastutena prasthānena sākṣāttadanuguṇaṃ ripukartṛkaṃ sūryamaṇḍalabhedanaṃ kāryaṃ gamyate //
body.translated_text: Here, in the context of describing the sun, which is presented as the subject (<s>varṇya</s>) for generating fear as a subsidiary to the description of the king — through the [sun's] departure, which is the unpresented [subject] (<s>aprastuta</s>) not directly appropriate to the presented [subject], the effect that is directly appropriate — namely the breaking of the solar disc by the enemy [i.e., the king's superiority over the sun] — is implied. //

children.text: āyātā kamalāsanasya bhavanāddraṣṭuṃ trilokītalaṃ gīrvāṇeṣu dināni kānicidaho nītvā punaḥ kautukāt /
children.translated_text: Having come from the abode of the Lotus-seated one (<s>Brahmā</s>) to behold the surface of the triple world, having spent some days among the gods, and then again out of curiosity,

children.text: bhrāntvā bhūvalaye mahākavikulopāsyā tavāsyāmbuje rājansaṃprati satyadhāmani girāṃ devī sukhaṃ vartate || 16 ||
children.translated_text: Having wandered about the terrestrial sphere, the Goddess of Speech (<s>Girāṃ Devī</s>), worshipped by the lineage of great poets, now dwells happily in the lotus of your face, O King, in the abode of truth (<s>Satyadhāman</s>). // <s>JPran</s>_16 //
Here, because of the relation of one placed-upon-thing to multiple substrates, [this is] <s>paryāya</s> (succession). //

Therein, the locative case in the first quarter — through the fifth case [ablative] that denotes the limit of separation [from Brahmā's abode] — since the separation presupposes proximity (<s>upaśleṣa</s>), the proximity-based locative is understood by implication (<s>ākṣepa</s>).

In '<s>Satyadhāman</s>' (abode of truth) — through the determination of non-difference (<s>abhedādhyavasāna</s>) based on <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia), the face being established as the realm of truth (<s>Satyaloka</s>), the comfortable dwelling [of the Goddess of Speech] is established. //

Is he the three-formed [deity] (<s>Trimūrti</s>) [that is] the darkness of the wretchedness of the learned, or the forest-fire of the grove of the lineage of hostile <s>Indras</s>, or perhaps the milk-ocean of the cool-rayed [moon] of his supremely radiant fame?

children.text: kiṃ vānaṅgabhujaṃgadaṣṭavanitājīvāturevaṃ nṛṇāṃ keṣāmeṣa narādhipo na janayatyalpetarāḥ kalpanāḥ || 17 ||
children.translated_text: Or does this sovereign not give rise to manifold fancies, great and small, in which people — like women bitten by the serpent of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the bodiless god of love) — [are like] physicians [trying to save] lives? // <s>JPran</s>_17 //

Here, because the [different] alternatives are based on successive superimpositions, [this is] a chain-doubt (<s>paramparita-saṃśaya</s>), and it is contrived (<s>āhārya</s>), since the root superimposition is of that nature.
Because there is no contradiction in contrived cognition even in a perceiver other than the poet — [that is, the perceiver] fashioned by the poet, [this] is acceptable as kāvya. //

children.text: nadanti madadantinaḥ parilasanti vājivrajāḥ paṭhanti birudāvalīmahitamandire bandinaḥ /
children.translated_text: The maddened elephants trumpet, the troops of horses prance, the bards recite the celebrated series of titles in the honored hall.

children.text: idaṃ tadavadhi prabho yadavadhi pravṛddhā na te yugāntadahanopamā nayanakoṇaśoṇadyutiḥ || 18 ||
children.translated_text: O Lord, this [is the state] only since [the time] that the reddish glow at the corner of your eye — comparable to the fire at the end of an age — has not intensified. // <s>JPran</s>_18 //

body.text: atra mukhyārthasya rājaviṣayāyāḥ kaviraterupakārakasya yadaiva tava kopodayastadaiva tava ripūṇāṃ saṃpado bhasmasādbhaviṣyantīti vastuna upakārikā nayanakoṇaśoṇadyuteryugāntadahanopamā //
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>upamā</s> (simile) comparing the reddish glow at the corner of the eye with the fire of universal dissolution is a helper (<s>upakārikā</s>) to the content (<s>vastu</s>), which is the helper of the primary meaning [pertaining to] the king — namely [the sense that] 'the very moment your anger arises, the wealth of your enemies will be reduced to ashes.' //

children.text: mayi tvadupamāvidhau vasumatīśa vācaṃyame na varṇayati māmayaṃ kaviriti krudhaṃ mā kṛthāḥ /
children.translated_text: O Lord of the earth, O master of speech — when I undertake the composition of a simile for you, do not be angry [thinking] 'this poet does not describe me [adequately].'

children.text: carācaramidaṃ jagajjanayato vidhermānase padaṃ na vidadhetarāṃ tava samo dvitīyo naraḥ || 19 ||
children.translated_text: In the mind of <s>Vidhi</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), who creates this world of moving and unmoving beings, a second man equal to you could not possibly find a place! // <s>JPran</s>_19 //

body.text: atra tvatsamo 'nyo nāstīti pratyayādupamānaluptopamā vyaṅgyeti prāñcaḥ /

children.translated_text: Since equality cannot be established in any way whatsoever, this is not an <s>upamā</s> [at all].
Otherwise, even <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) would have the same [unwarranted] consequence.
'Searching among the thorn-tangled, narrow pathways,
O bee, buzzing about, you will not find [a flower] resembling the garland-blossom.'

body.translated_text: Here, from the cognition 'there is no other equal to you,' [this is] an <s>upamā</s> (simile) with the standard of comparison suppressed (<s>upamāna-lupta</s>) that is suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) — according to the ancients.

children.text: '; ityatra tu na prāpsyasītyuktvā kvacittvadagocare sthale bhaviṣyatīti pratīteḥ sādṛśyapratiṣṭhānālluptopamāstu /
children.translated_text: Here, however, since by saying 'you will not find,' the understanding arises that [the standard of comparison] will exist somewhere beyond your reach, there is an establishment of similarity — hence [this is] a simile with suppression (<s>luptopamā</s>).
Therefore, this [verse JPran_19] is not an <s>alaṃkāra</s> at all — so say the moderns. //
You who shatter the tusked elephants of [your enemies'] pride with whirling battle-axes wielded by [your] arms — beholding you, O crusher of the circle of foes, in battle,

children.text: karālakuliśāhatisphuṭavibhinnavindhyācalo na kasya hṛdayaṃ jhaṭityadhiruroha jambhāhitaḥ || 20 ||
children.translated_text: Was there anyone into whose heart <s>Jambhāhiti</s> (<s>Indra</s>), [with images of] the <s>Vindhya</s> mountain split open by the blows of his fearsome thunderbolt, did not suddenly ascend? // <s>JPran</s>_20 //

body.translated_text: Here [the figure is] <s>smaraṇa</s> (recollection); however, [it is] implicit (<s>lakṣya</s>). //

children.text: yamaḥ pratimahībhṛtāṃ hutavaho 'si tannīvṛtāṃ satāṃ khalu yudhiṣṭhiro dhanapatirdhanākāṅkṣiṇām /
children.translated_text: You are <s>Yama</s> to opposing kings, the sacrificial fire to their retinues, indeed <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> to the virtuous, <s>Dhanapati</s> (<s>Kubera</s>) to those who desire wealth,

children.text: gṛhaṃ śaraṇamicchatāṃ kuliśakoṭibhirnirmitaṃ tvameka iha bhūtale bahuvidho vidhātrā kṛtaḥ || 21 ||
children.translated_text: A house forged with thunderbolt-tips for those who seek shelter — you alone on this earth have been made multiform by the Creator (<s>Vidhātṛ</s>)! // <s>JPran</s>_21 //

body.text: atra kavinā yamatvādinā rūpeṇa rājño rūpavataḥ karaṇādrūpakeṇa vipakṣabhūpālādīnāmetasminnāgate yamatvādinā bhrānterapi saṃbhavādbhrāntimatā tairevānekairgrahītṛbhiranekairdharmairullekhanādullekhaviśeṣeṇa ca saha saṃkīrṇo 'pi saṃbandhiṣaṣṭhyantabhedaprayuktavarṇyānekavidhatvaka ullekhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Here, through the <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), by which the king as subject is endowed with forms such as <s>Yama</s>-hood etc. by the poet — since there is the possibility of a delusion (<s>bhrānti</s>) regarding the hostile kings etc. that <s>Yama</s>-hood etc. actually belongs to this one — combined with the <s>bhrāntimat</s> [figure], this is an <s>ullekha</s> (variant perception) combined [with other figures], due to the subject being perceived through multiple properties by multiple perceivers, and due to the multiplicity of the described subject produced by the [different] relational genitives. //

children.text: dvinetra iva vāsavo mitakaro vivasvāniva dvitīya iva candramāḥ śritavapurmanobhūriva /
children.translated_text: Like <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>) with two eyes, like <s>Vivasvān</s> (the Sun) with measured hands, like a second Moon, like the mind-born one (<s>Manobhū</s> / <s>Kāmadeva</s>) having assumed a body,

Like the ocean in human form, like a <s>guru</s> (teacher / <s>Bṛhaspati</s>) who has descended to the earth — saluted by all <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the Lord of <s>Kāmarūpa</s> is victorious! // <s>JPran</s>_22 //

body.text:
atra rājagatānāṃ dvinetratvādīnāṃ vāsavāditādātmyavirodhināṃ virodhanivartanāya viṣayiṣu vāsavādiṣvāropeṇa sādhāraṇīkaraṇāttannimittakotprekṣā /
sā ceha mālārūpā /
na cātropamā śakyarūpaṇā /

children.translated_text: Because the statement of two-eyedness etc. would be rendered purposeless [in a simile].

children.text: na copamāniṣpādakaṃ teṣāṃ sādhāraṇyaṃ tadabhāve 'pi paramaiśvaryādibhiḥ pratīyamānaistasyā niṣpatteḥ /
children.translated_text: Nor is the commonality [between king and gods] that produces the simile [present] — since even in the absence of that [commonality], the simile would be accomplished through the perceived [qualities of] supreme sovereignty etc.
And because the poet does not intend it as producing a simile, since [the commonality through] unbeautiful [properties like two-eyedness] would make the simile unappealing.

children.text: evaṃ dvitīyādīnāṃ candrādiṣvāropo 'pyupamāyāṃ satyāmanarthaka eva syāt //
children.translated_text: Similarly, the superimposition of 'second' etc. onto the Moon etc. would also be pointless if a simile were [intended]. //

body.translated_text:
Here, in order to remove the contradiction between the properties of the king — such as having two eyes etc. — and the identity with <s>Vāsava</s> etc. [who have different numbers of eyes, etc.], by superimposing [those properties] onto the [respective] referents <s>Vāsava</s> etc. [thereby] making them common, [this is] an <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) based on that [commonality].
And this is here in the form of a garland (<s>mālā</s>).
An <s>upamā</s> (simile) cannot be postulated here,

children.text: dīnavrāte dayārdrā nikhilaripukule nirdayā kiṃ ca mṛdvī kāvyālāpeṣu tarkaprativacanavidhau karkaśatvaṃ dadhānā /
children.translated_text: Compassionate toward the wretched multitude, merciless toward the entire host of enemies; gentle in the conversation of poetry, yet harsh in the procedure of logical counter-argument;

children.text: lubdhā dharmeṣvalubdhā vasuni paravipaddarśane kāṃdiśīkā rājannājanmaramya sphurati bahuvidhā tāvakī cittavṛttiḥ || 23 ||
children.translated_text: Greedy for <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), ungreedy for material wealth; bewildered at the sight of others' misfortune — O King, from birth itself, your manifold mental disposition shines forth in many aspects! // <s>JPran</s>_23 //
Here, because the mental disposition is manifold due to the multiplicity of objects — [this is] <s>ullekha</s> (variant perception).
And therein, the determination of unity as being his mental disposition is the underlying principle (<s>tantra</s>). //

children.text: devāḥ ke pūrvadevāḥ samiti mama naraḥ santi ke vā purastādeva jalpanti tāvatpratibhaṭapṛtanāvartinaḥ kṣatravīrāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Who are the gods? Who are the ancient gods? Are there any men before me?' — thus boast the warrior heroes who advance against the opposing army,

As long as your sword — a serpent that feeds on the fresh milk of the life-breaths of charming foes, whose form terrifies <s>Antaka</s> (Death himself) — has not yet come within the range of their sight, O King! // <s>JPran</s>_24 //

body.translated_text: Here [the figure is] a pure chain-metaphor (<s>śuddha-paramparita-rūpaka</s>). //

children.translated_text: The luster of the crest-jewel of dignity of the great jewel of the day (the Sun) rising at the eastern horizon; the terrible garland of flames of the fire of wrath at the end of time that has swallowed the world;

children.text: āśākāntāpadāmbhoruhatalavigalanmañjulākṣārasābhā sā bhāti kṣoṇiśobhākaraṇa tava dṛśoḥ saṃgare śoṇimaśrīḥ || 25 ||
children.translated_text: The beautiful glow like lac-dye flowing from the soles of the lotus-feet of the beloved of the directions — that crimson splendor of your eyes in battle shines forth, O you who beautify the earth! // <s>JPran</s>_25 //

body.translated_text: Here too [the figure is] the same [chain-metaphor], but in garland form (<s>mālātmaka</s>). //

children.translated_text: Beholding you in battle, O sole connoisseur of banishing the harsh pride of confidence from the assemblage of beautiful women [i.e., the royal fortunes of enemies],

children.text: kā vā ripukṣitibhṛtāṃ bata rājalakṣmīḥ svāmivratatvamapariskhalitaṃ babhāra || 26 ||
children.translated_text: Which royal fortune (<s>rājalakṣmī</s>) of the enemy kings, alas, maintained her vow of fidelity to her lord (<s>svāmivratya</s>) without stumbling? // <s>JPran</s>_26 //

children.text: atra śatrūṇāṃ rājyalakṣmīstvāṃ prāpteti vivakṣito 'rthaḥ pātivratyaskhalitarūpeṇābhihita iti paryāyoktam /
children.translated_text: Here the intended meaning — that the royal fortunes of the enemies came to you — is expressed in the form of a lapse of fidelity (<s>pātivratyaskhaliata</s>); hence [this is] <s>paryāyokta</s> (indirect expression).

children.text: tacca rājyalakṣmyā nāyikātvasiddhyarthaṃ samāsoktimapekṣata iti sā tatra guṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: And that [<s>paryāyokta</s>] requires <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) for the purpose of establishing the royal fortune (<s>rājyalakṣmī</s>) as a heroine (<s>nāyikā</s>) — hence that [<s>samāsokti</s>] is a subordinate element (<s>guṇa</s>) therein. //

children.text: nāsatyayogo vacaneṣu kīrtau tathārjunaḥ karmaṇi cāpi dharmaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no conjunction with falsehood in [your] words; in fame, there is indeed <s>Arjuna</s> (whiteness/the hero); in action too, there is <s>dharma</s> (righteousness);

children.text: citte jagatprāṇabhavo yadāste vaśaṃvadāste kimu pānḍuputrāḥ || 27 ||
children.translated_text: When the world-enlivening one (<s>Jagatprāṇabhava</s> / <s>Bhīma</s>) resides in [your] heart — are the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> not then obedient to you? // <s>JPran</s>_27 //

body.text: atra pāṇḍuputreṣu viṣayeṣu rājavaśaṃvadatādātmyotprekṣāyāṃ rājāśritatvarūpo viṣayidharmaḥ śleṣeṇa viṣayāṇāṃ tadāśritānāṃ cāsatyābhāvaśuklagunapuṇyaparameśvarāṇāmabhedasaṃpādanadvārā viṣayasādhāraṇīkṛtaḥ //
body.translated_text: Here, in the <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) that the <s>Pāṇḍu</s> sons, who are the referents, are obedient to the king as their master — the property of the referent, namely being dependent on the king, is made common to the referents through <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia), by which the non-difference of the referents [the five Pāṇḍava qualities] — <s>Asatya</s> (non-falsehood), <s>Śukla</s> (whiteness), <s>Guṇa</s> (virtue), <s>Puṇya</s> (merit), <s>Parameśvara</s> (supreme lord) — which are dependent on them, is achieved. //

children.translated_text: The minute drops of nectar that fell from the milk-ocean, subject to the force of the churning of Mount <s>Manthāra</s> (<s>Mandara</s>) —
With those [drops], having become one with various herbs, the Creator (<s>Dhātṛ</s>) fashioned, O Lord, the ends of your compassionate glances. // <s>JPran</s>_28 //

body.text: atra dṛganteṣu na kevalaṃ saṃjīvakatvādayo 'mṛtamātraguṇa eva kaverbubodhayiṣitā api tu nikhilajanavaśīkāratvādayo 'nye 'pīti sudhākaṇeṣvoṣadhīsaṃsargo 'tiśayārthamupāttaḥ //
body.translated_text: Here the poet wished to convey not merely the qualities of nectar alone, such as the power of reviving, in the sidelong glances, but also other qualities such as the power to subjugate all people. Therefore, the association with medicinal herbs in the drops of nectar is employed for the purpose of intensification.

children.translated_text: Together with the hair of young women, with the entire treasuries, and with the very lives of rival kings,

children.text: tvayā raṇe niṣkaruṇena gāḍhaṃ cāpasya jīvā cakṛṣe javena || 29 ||
children.translated_text: you, merciless in battle, forcefully drew the bowstring with speed. || 29 ||

body.translated_text: Here, <s>sahokti</s> (concurrent expression) is enlivened by the intensification consisting of the reversal of the temporal sequence of the effects of drawing the bow, such as the pulling of hair and the like.

children.text: mahendratulyaṃ kavayo bhavantaṃ vadantu kiṃ tāniha vārayāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: Let the poets call you equal to great <s>Indra</s>—shall we indeed prevent them?
But you, worshipped by thousands, how can you be equal to the lord of the gods? || 30 ||

body.translated_text: Here, <s>vyatireka</s> (dissimilarity) is employed with dual foundation, taking up the number of thirty [gods] raised through <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia).

children.text: sa tu varṣatu vāri vāridastvamudārāśaya ratnavarṣaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Let that cloud rain water—you, of generous mind, rain jewels.
That one is dark with the grime of the new-moon night—you are pure both within and without. || 31 ||

body.text: atrāpi sa eva paraṃ tu śleṣo 'trānutthāpako niṣidhyamānaṃ sāmyaṃ ca na śābdamiti viśeṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: Here too the same [figure applies], but the distinction is that the <s>śleṣa</s> here is non-evocative, and the similarity being denied is not merely verbal.

children.translated_text: By some he was judged to be a lord of men; by others, he was reckoned a lord of wealth.

children.text: ajani kevalameṣa girāṃ patirbhuvi madekamate kamateśvaraḥ || 32 ||
children.translated_text: He was born on earth simply as this lord of speech—my sole conviction—the lord of <s>Kāma</s>. || 32 ||

children.text: atra nāyaṃ rājā kiṃ tu girāṃ patirityākārāpahnutiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, "this one is not a king, but a lord of speech"—this is <s>ākārāpahnuti</s> (denial of the real form).
The part of denial therein is understood from the first half through the expression of the ultimate truth.
The part of superimposition, however, is from the second half.
Accompanied by great warriors resembling crocodiles and by poets resembling jewels,
you, O lord of the earth, are the receptacle of the poetry-nectar and the moon of fame. || 33 ||

children.text: atra rājño jaladhyupamāyāḥ śabdenābhidhāne 'pyaṅgopamābhirākṣepādekadeśavivartinyupamā tenottarārdha upamitasamāsa eva /
children.translated_text: Here, even though the king's resemblance to the ocean is verbally stated, because it is evoked by the component similes, it is a simile that transforms part of itself. Therefore in the second half there is only a compound of things compared.
Because the identity conveyed by the qualifying compound is not relevant to the subject.
Before the enemy kings, O beloved of the earth, they are first reduced to ashes,
and immediately after, from the arch of your frown, sparks of the fire of anger fall. || 34 ||
Here, the intensification of the swiftness of the effect is to be understood as caused by the intensification of the agent.
And this is <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) in the form of reversal of the temporal sequence of cause and effect.
In all three worlds, filled with humans, gods, and demons,

children.text: na bhaviṣyati nāsti nābhavannṛpa yaste bhajate tulāspadam || 35 ||
children.translated_text: there has not been, is not, and shall not be, O king, anyone who occupies a place on your scale [of comparison]. || 35 ||
Here, the ancients [call this] <s>upamānaluptopamā</s> (simile with the standard of comparison removed).
But we [call it] <s>asamākhya</s> (the inexpressible)—a different figure of speech.
Even a small utterance of yours, resembling the broth of nectar, once drunk,
the excess of sweetness from the lip-fruit of women does not suffice for satisfaction. || 36 ||
Here, a variety of <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole): asserting non-relation where there is relation.

children.text: upameyopamānaviśeṣaṇābhyāmalpatvodriktatvābhyāmalpayāpi saha bhūyānapi madhurimā sāmyaṃ kartuṃ yatrānīśastatra kiṃ vācyaṃ bhūyasyeti vailakṣaṇyātmā vyatirekaśca //
children.translated_text: From the qualifiers of the compared and the standard of comparison, namely smallness and abundance—that even abundance of sweetness is unable to equal even a small [utterance]—from this incongruity there is also <s>vyatireka</s> (dissimilarity).
Abiding in the sky, it illuminates the entire world and causes the night-lily to bloom;
your fame, residing on earth, brings the sons of <s>Sagara</s> to the state of equal fruition. || 37 ||

body.translated_text: Here, there is <s>ullekhadhvani</s> (suggestive tracing) combined with a <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) in the form of moonlight being suggested.

children.translated_text: You rise from your seat, filled with anger, together with the fortune of your enemies;

children.text: sahasaiva patasi teṣu kṣitiśāsana mṛtyunā sākam || 38 ||
children.translated_text: suddenly you fall upon them, O ruler of the earth, together with death. || 38 ||
In the verse "with the hair of young women," the <s>sahokti</s> (concurrent expression) pertains to the object.
But here the distinction is that it pertains to the agent.
When you, equal to <s>Pākaśāsana</s> (<s>Indra</s>), rule the entire circle of the earth,

children.text: vipine vairivadhūnāṃ varṣanti vilocanāni ca dināni || 39 ||
children.translated_text: in the forest, the eyes of the enemy's women rain [tears] and their days [are gloomy]. || 39 ||
Here, through the <s>kvip</s>-suffix participial form meaning "acting like rain," there is <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal conjunction) based on <s>śleṣa</s>, arising from <s>śleṣa</s>.
Because both the standard of comparison and the thing compared are relevant to the subject, as pertaining to the description of the enemies' women.
O lord of men, he in whose hand you, the medicine for removing the harm of enemies, are held—
how can there be fear of serpents for him, even as he traverses the entire earth? || 40 ||

body.text: atra śleṣaniveditasya sarpabhayābhāvasyopapādakatayopāttasya rājani bheṣajatādātmyāropasyāpyupapādakatayā sthitaṃ rājasaṃbandhini dviṣadapakaraṇarūpe dharme śleṣaniveditasarpatāpakaraṇatādātmyamiti prathamacaraṇe śliṣṭaparamparitarūpakaṃ tṛtīye tu śleṣa eva /
body.translated_text: Here, the absence of fear of serpents communicated through <s>śleṣa</s>, being employed as a corroboration, and the superimposition of the identity of medicine upon the king also standing as a corroboration—thus the identity with the removal of harm to enemies, which is the attribute related to the king, with the removal of serpent-venom communicated through <s>śleṣa</s>, constitutes <s>śliṣṭaparamparita-rūpaka</s> (extended concatenated metaphor through paronomasia) in the first quarter, while in the third there is simply <s>śleṣa</s>.

children.text: kuvalayalakṣmīṃ harate tava kīrtistatra kiṃ citram /
children.translated_text: Your fame steals the beauty of the blue lotus—what wonder is there in that?
For you, whose lotus-feet are bowed to by the world, are indeed the source of this [beauty]. || 41 ||
Here, because the producer has qualities identical to [those of] the product, there is a special figure of conformity of the product with the association of the producer.
And in this, <s>śleṣa</s> is a subordinate quality.
If seen in the assembly, [you are like] fierce moonlight, sandalwood, and moon-beams;
but you in battle [are like] gentle fire of the end-times and <s>Śeṣa</s> (the cosmic serpent). || 42 ||

children.text: atra dṛṣṭaḥ sadasīti vākye tvamityasyāpakarṣaṇāt, atha tvaṃ saṃgara ityatra ca tvamityasyānuvartanādvākyayoḥ padavinimayātmālaṃkāraḥ pūrvārdhe /
children.translated_text: Here, in the statement "seen in the assembly," because "you" is drawn away, and in "but you in battle," because "you" carries over, the figure consists of the exchange of words between the two sentences in the first half.
In the second half, there is <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal conjunction) due to the connection with multiple attributes of the subject.

This is variegated with another figure, consisting of attributing to the standard of comparison qualities contrary to those of the thing compared, for the purpose of establishing the superior qualities of the thing compared.
In the boundless <s>saṃsāra</s>, fate made only one <s>Arjuna</s>;

children.text: kīrtyā nirmalayā bhūpa tvayā sarve 'rjunāḥ kṛtāḥ || 43 ||
children.translated_text: but you, O king, with your spotless fame, have made everyone <s>Arjuna</s> (bright/white). || 43 ||

body.translated_text: Here, <s>vyatireka</s> (dissimilarity) is based on <s>śleṣa</s>.

children.translated_text: In [comparison with] <s>Dadhīci</s>, <s>Bali</s>, <s>Karṇa</s>, the <s>Himālaya</s>, the golden mountain, and the ocean,
the quality of non-giving and lack of steadfastness is seen and shines [when you are beheld]. || 44 ||
Here too, the same type [of figure applies].
But the distinction is the intermixture of <s>yathāsaṃkhya</s> (enumeration in order).
When you, O king, rule the undivided circle of the earth,
not even in the slightest are the circles of enemies and friends at ease. || 45 ||

body.translated_text: Here too there is <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal conjunction) raised through the <s>śleṣa</s> of the word <s>mitra</s> (friend/sun), and also <s>vyājastuti</s> (praise through irony).

children.translated_text: Is he <s>Bhānu</s> (the Sun), <s>Agni</s> (Fire), <s>Yama</s> (Death), <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind), <s>Bali</s>, <s>Karṇa</s>, or <s>Śibi</s>?
Thus adversaries and supplicants fall into doubt regarding you. || 46 ||

body.translated_text: Here, <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt) is embraced by <s>ullekha</s> (tracing).

children.translated_text: You are the lake that is the abode of <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), the lord of serpents who embodies patience and steadfastness;
you, the moon of the blue lotus [world], delight mankind. || 47 ||

body.translated_text: Here, <s>śliṣṭaparamparita rūpaka</s> (extended concatenated metaphor through paronomasia) in garland form.

children.translated_text: In the sky, your fames become moonlight; on the snowy mountain, they become snow;
on the earth, O king, they become the ocean. || 48 ||

body.translated_text: Here, <s>ullekha</s> (tracing) embraced by <s>mālopamā</s> (garland-simile).

children.translated_text: Bestowing deer-hood upon [rival kings], and tree-hood upon [their houses], making them like sandalwood trees,
you, O king, are the moon among the kings of the earth. || 49 ||
Here, pure <s>paramparitā</s> (concatenated) garland-form simile.
Through the <s>kvip</s>-suffix participial, the forms in the nominal [part],
and one in the verbal form [<s>indavasi</s>, 'you are the moon'].
In the midst of a nectar-ocean, in the interior of a house made of whiteness,
on a seat of the full moon, O lord, your utterances are worthy to abide. || 50 ||

body.text: atra trayāṇāṃ sudhāsamudrādīnāṃ viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvena madhurimaṇi parāṃ kāṣṭhāmadhirūḍhe tvadīyoktipadasaṃbandho yukto na tu viśakalita ityatiśāyakāsadviśeṣaṇanibandhanaḥ prauḍhoktiḥ //
body.translated_text: Here, the relation of the words to your utterances is appropriate when the three—the nectar-ocean and the others—as qualifier and qualified have ascended to the highest degree of sweetness; but not when they are separated. Therefore, this is <s>prauḍhokti</s> (bold expression) based on an intense qualifying superlative.

children.translated_text: From you who have subordinated the waves of nectar, the moonlight, and the lotus-faces of <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>)—from you, a boundless ocean of grace,

children.text: ubhayavadayaṃ deva tvattaḥ kathaṃ paramolbaṇaḥ pralayadahanajvālājālākulo mahasāṃ gaṇaḥ || 51 ||
children.translated_text: O lord, how did this extremely terrible assemblage of splendors, turbulent with the flames of the fire of dissolution, [arise] from you, who are of both natures? || 51 ||
Here, the production of an effect whose own qualities are contrary to the qualities of the cause constitutes the figure <s>viṣama</s> (incongruity).

Through <s>vyatireka</s> (dissimilarity) in the form of the subordination of the three—the waves of nectar and others—the intensification of the qualities of life-giving power, supreme coolness, purity, and beauty is understood.
Thus, other figures that may be found in these verses have not been analyzed due to their obviousness.
Something has been explained for the delight of the connoisseurs as was necessary; the rest is to be illuminated by them alone—enough of elaboration.

The illustrious <s>Paṇḍitarāja Paṇḍita Jagannātha</s>, son of the venerable <s>Peramabhaṭṭa</s>, graciously attended by the great <s>Lakṣmī</s> who is the auspicious jewel of the <s>Tailaṅga</s> lineage, a perpetual brilliance on the brow of the learned,

children.text: saṃtuṣṭaḥ kamatādhipasya kavitāmākarṇya tadvarṇanaṃ śrīmatpaṇḍitarājapaṇḍitajagannātho vyadhāsīdidam || 52 ||
children.translated_text: having heard with satisfaction the poetry of the lord of <s>Kamata</s>, composed this description of it. || 52 ||
Beholding you in the midst of battle, with your pair of arm-staffs coiling the resplendent bow, and with fierce arrows having destroyed the host of brazen enemies—

What king would not remember the great festival of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, delighted by the shower from <s>Khāṇḍava</s> [forest], falling [in ashes] from the wild dance of the ring of flames of arrows released from the leaping <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> [bow]? || 53 ||
Here, the figure of speech is <s>smaraṇālaṃkāra</s> (the figure of remembrance).
But one should not be misled [into thinking this is] a <s>bhāva</s> (emotional state).

Because the distinction between <s>bhāva</s> (emotional state) and <s>alaṃkāra</s> (figure of speech) is established here on the basis of whether it is grounded in resemblance or not so grounded, and because it is cognizable through [its own] word. //

body.text: iti paṇḍitarājaśrījagannāthaviracitaṃ prāṇābharaṇaṃ tatkṛtayaiva ṭippaṇyā sametaṃ samāptam /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Prāṇābharaṇa</s>, composed by <s>Paṇḍitarāja Śrī Jagannātha</s>, together with the annotation (<s>ṭippaṇī</s>) by him alone.
